correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly derives channel parity, nonzero amplitudes by Legendre double-factorial identities, discrete Fourier rank-one equivalence classes, exact odd/even cardinalities, and full-rank sharp extrema from monotonic factorial ratios. Every quantifier is handled analytically, including ℓ=1 and arbitrary M. A standalone checker independently reproduced all finite tested cases, without treating them as a proof of the unbounded claim.

originality.rationale: Material full-text and semantic comparisons of general gradient-augmented reconstruction, randomized spherical-value recovery, multiple-ring low-pass sampling, regular-grid Wigner sensing and the nearest published exact sampling spectra show no statement logically covering the fixed-degree S^2 equatorial two-channel first-jet rank, complete block spectrum and sharp conditioning theorem. The parity-aliased Fourier argument is elementary prior machinery and is not itself claimed as new. Remaining risk: earlier unindexed Hermite/Cauchy sampling treatments.
residual_risks: An unindexed or terminologically different theorem for equatorial normal-derivative harmonic sampling might give an equivalent statement.

Generic harmonic separation formulas allow the present conclusion to be derived, but this is not evidence the exact global claim is already stated; independent historical-priority evaluation remains outstanding.

value.rationale: Equatorial values and normal derivatives are the natural Cauchy first jet for a fixed spherical Laplace eigenmode. The exact parity-dependent minimum node count and full spectral aliasing diagnosis supply a meaningful acquisition tradeoff, and the sharp noise amplification ratio (ℓ+1)/2 and independence from oversampling are precise recovery properties absent from the nearest value-only results.
